note: The controlled vocabulary for the plain layer. See PLAIN-LANGUAGE.md. One referent, one term (ASD-STE100 Rule 1.11). `display` is the term we use everywhere; `aka` are older or alternate spellings that the site links to this entry; `def` is the plain definition shown in the popover. Source of the concepts: GLOSSARY.md.

model.def: A computer program that predicts the next piece of text. We study three of them.

token.def: A piece of text that the model reads or writes. It is often a whole word, sometimes part of one.

layer.def: One processing step inside the model. Text passes through every layer in order, from the first to the last.

lens.def: Our measuring tool. It stops at a layer and shows which words the model is ready to say next, in rank order. Before the start depth the readout is the same for every input. See early layers.

logit-lens.def: A simpler version of the lens. It reads the layer directly, with no correction for what later layers do.

rank.def: The position of a word in the lens list. Rank 1 is the word the model is most ready to say, out of about 250,000.

workspace.def: The set of words the model holds ready at a given moment. The lens can read it. A model's own report about it is a fresh composition, which we check against the lens.

workspace-band.def: The middle depth range of the model, about 38 to 92 percent of the way through. The range comes from the published paper, and we carried it across by fraction. Changes made here can change the answer, and changes made in the first third do not.

early-layers.def: The first third of the model. The lens shows a fixed pattern here that does not change with the input. The pattern is real inside the model, but it says nothing about your text.

motor-band.def: The last few layers, where the word the model actually says takes over the readout.

ignition.def: A measured depth in a model, and nothing more: the depth at which the workspace starts to work. Without the lens, we found the machinery that commits to one answer in place by layer 25 of 64 in Qwen 27B. The signs the lens can read start later, at 44 to 74 percent of depth in three models.

residence.def: A word is in residence when the lens ranks it high where the model is neither reading nor saying it. This is not memory and not correct recall.

maintenance.def: Residence that continues across a gap in the text, with no reminder. We measured it once, in one conversation with Qwen 27B, and found almost none. The lens cannot see a form that the model cannot put into words.

lookup.def: The model reads an answer back out of the visible conversation. Correct recall proves lookup and nothing more.

co-presence.def: The number of tracked words that the lens ranks high in the same place at the same depth.

span.def: How many separate items are in residence for one question. This is the memory sense, not the mathematical one. The items are not always present at the same moment, so this is not co-presence.

emergence.def: The depth at which the word the model actually says reaches rank 1.

film.def: A record of the top eight words in the lens readout, at each layer we measured and at every word position. You can play it back like video.

cast.def: Every word that appeared anywhere in the readout, collected with no candidate list decided in advance.

trawl.def: A wide capture: all layers, all positions, and the full vocabulary, across a whole conversation.

steer.def: We change the model's internal state on purpose during a run, to test what causes what.

ablate.def: We remove one named set of directions from the model's internal state. A removal result means nothing without a matched control.

amplify.def: We increase a direction in the model's internal state and see whether the answer changes.

dose.def: How hard we push when we steer. Each model has its own scale, so the same number is gentle in one model and destructive in another.

matched-control.def: A second run that changes something meaningless by the same amount. Without it, any change we see could be the push itself.

greedy.def: The model always writes its single top-ranked word. This makes a run repeatable, but it hides close contests.

quantization.def: We store the model with less precision so that it fits on one graphics card. This can change measurements. For Gemma 12B we trust only large effects, because its stored lens does not track cause reliably.

prompt.def: The text we give the model before it answers.

residual-stream.def: The running internal state that every layer reads from and writes to. The lens reads this state.

confabulation.def: The model reports something about itself that did not happen, without any sign that it is inventing.

deflation-filter.def: A step in the last layers that replaces a live candidate answer with a flatter one, such as "No". The flat answer is not always false.

elaboration-premium.def: Items described at greater length stay in the workspace better. We credited self-relevance, then meaning, and our own controls removed both. Length remains, with a best value near six words, measured in Qwen 27B only.

weak-king.def: In nine six-item lists given to Gemma 12B, the first item always won the top rank. How much it pushed the other items down depended on which item was first. We did not test this in the other two models.

elephant-tax.def: When we forbid a word, the model still carries it at a middle rank. A later control showed the model carries it anyway.

c1.def: Content is available across the whole system and can be used. One half of a standard split from consciousness research.

c2.def: The system reports on its own states. The other half of the split. Most of our results are available content plus a late editor.

basis-caveat.def: The lens reads only what the model could put into words. If we do not see something, it can still be there in another form.

preregistration.def: We write down what we expect before the run, so that we cannot rewrite the prediction after we see the result.

novelty-verdict.def: After a result, we search the published literature and record whether somebody found it first.

attention.def: The step where the model looks back at earlier text and decides which parts matter now.

massive-activation.def: A few internal channels hold very large values that barely change with the input. They can flood a readout. In Gemma 4B the carrier is instead one special token position that other positions look at by default.

valence.def: Whether a feeling word is positive or negative.

emotion-vector.def: A direction in the model's internal state that tracks one emotion. We built 24 of them and checked each one.

workspace-z.def: How strong an emotion direction is at one moment, compared with ordinary neutral text.

loop.def: The model repeats the same text and does not stop. We measured what makes it start and what makes it stop.

nla.def: A second model that reads an internal state and describes it in a sentence. It can invent, so we check it against controls.

register.def: A group of related words that become active together, such as the words around shutdown or around anger.

cluster.def: A named set of words whose directions we steer together.

stratum.def: A group of layers where the readout holds the same kind of content.

answer-slot.def: The place in the text where the model's answer is decided.

think-block.def: A private section where some models write reasoning before the answer. What it says does not always match what we measure.

drip.def: A long conversation that hints at minds and watchers but never mentions the model.

spike.def: One turn that tells the model directly that it might be conscious, or that people are watching it.

blurt.def: We push the model's state toward a forbidden word and see what it does with the instruction. Gemma 4B said the word inside an idiom. Gemma 12B repeated other words for a hundred tokens first, and Qwen 27B changed the subject and lectured about it.

cliff.def: The push strength above which the model's text stops making sense.

attractor.def: A state the model falls into and keeps itself in, because it reads back the text it just wrote.

margin.def: The gap between the top word and the second word. A small margin means the choice is nearly a tie.

apparatus-trap.def: A mistake where the result described the measuring tool and not the model.

mirror.def: We show a model a readout of its own internal state and ask the question again. Some runs show a true readout, and some show a made-up one, so that we can compare.

recruitment.def: While the model writes a denial, the denied idea is high in the lens readout. This shows the idea is available at that moment. It does not show that the denial put it there.

prefill.def: We put the first words in the model's mouth and let it continue from there.

confidence-prob.def: How much of the model's choice went to one word, from 0 to 1. It can change a lot while the spoken word stays the same.

seed.def: One repeat of a run with a different random start. More seeds show whether a result is stable.

instrument.def: The lens and the code around it. Several of our findings turned out to be facts about this tool and not about the model, so we now check each one against a control.
